drivingQuestion: Does a part of a carcass that one cannot touch through its protective covering impart impurity?
outcomeNote: Both 'if that is so' difficulties are answered on the facts, and Rav Oshaya resolves his own dilemma.

segments.he: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ נִיקְּבָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״הַנּוֹגֵעַ … יִטְמָא״, אֶת שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לִיגַּע – טָמֵא, וְאֶת שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִיגַּע – טָהוֹר.
segments.en: One «might» have thought that «even» one who touches «a perforated» thigh bone remains pure. Therefore, «the verse states: “One who touches» the carcass thereof [benivlatah] «shall be impure,”» indicating that one who touches a part of the animal through «which it is possible to touch» the flesh, which has the halakhic status of an unslaughtered carcass [neveila], is «impure, but» one who touches a part of the animal through «which it is impossible to touch» the flesh remains «pure.» Therefore, one who touches a protective layer such as the outside of a sealed thigh bone does not become impure, as it is impossible to touch the marrow.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְאַבָּיֵי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, בְּהֵמָה בְּעוֹרָהּ לֹא תְּטַמֵּא? פּוֹק חֲזִי כַּמָּה נְקָבִים יֵשׁ בָּהּ!
segments.en: «Rabbi Zeira said to Abaye: If that is so,» that one who touches the protective layer of a carcass via which it is impossible to touch the flesh of the carcass itself does not become impure, «an animal» still «in its hide should not impart impurity,» as one can touch the hide, which constitutes a protective layer, but not the flesh. Abaye answered: «Go out» and «see how many orifices there are in» the body of an animal via which one can touch the flesh, e.g., the eyes, the nostrils, and the mouth.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, כּוּלְיָא בְּחֶלְבָּהּ לֹא תְּטַמֵּא? תָּא חֲזִי כַּמָּה חוּטִין נִמְשָׁכִין הֵימֶנָּה.
segments.en: Similarly, «Rav Pappa said to Rava: If that is so,» that one who touches the protective layer of a carcass via which it is impossible to touch the flesh of the carcass itself does not become impure, «the kidney» of a carcass that is completely covered «in its fat should not impart impurity» via contact. Rava answered: «Come» and «see how many sinews emerge from» the kidney that one is able to touch.

segments.he: בָּעֵי רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: חִישֵּׁב עָלֶיהָ לְנוֹקְבָהּ וְלֹא נִיקְּבָה, מַהוּ? מְחוּסַּר נְקִיבָה כִּמְחוּסַּר מַעֲשֶׂה דָּמֵי, אוֹ לָא?
segments.en: §The mishna taught that the halakha distinguishes between a sealed and a perforated thigh bone of a carcass or a creeping animal. With regard to this topic, «Rav Oshaya raises a dilemma: What is» the halakha if «one intended to perforate» the thigh bone «but did not» yet «perforate it?» This is the dilemma: Is a thigh bone «lacking perforation considered to be lacking» the necessary «action» for it to impart impurity, and it therefore retains its status as a sealed thigh bone, «or not?»

segments.he: הֲדַר פַּשְׁטַהּ: מְחוּסַּר נְקִיבָה לָאו כִּמְחוּסַּר מַעֲשֶׂה דָּמֵי.
segments.en: Rabbi Oshaya «then resolves» the dilemma: A thigh bone «lacking perforation is not considered to be lacking» the necessary «action» for it to impart impurity. If one intends to perforate it, it imparts impurity immediately.

moves.summary: The baraita of the previous unit asks whether even a perforated bone leaves one pure.
moves.about: the baraita quotes one who touches ... shall be impure to fix the limit of carcass impurity

moves.summary: Scripture answers: what can be touched conveys impurity, what cannot does not.
moves.about: the verse limits carcass impurity to a part through which the flesh can actually be touched, so a perforated bone conveys impurity and a sealed one does not

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבי זירא לאביי: אלא מעתה
moves.summary: Rabbi Zeira presses Abaye: then a carcass still in its hide should convey nothing.
moves.about: whether the baraita's principle implies that a carcass still in its hide, whose flesh cannot be touched, imparts no impurity

moves.cueHe: פוק חזי כמה נקבים יש בה
moves.summary: Abaye: an animal is full of orifices through which the flesh is reachable.
moves.about: an animal in its hide has many orifices — eyes, nostrils, mouth — through which the flesh can be touched

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב פפא לרבא: אלא מעתה
moves.summary: Rav Pappa presses Rava with the parallel case of a kidney sealed in its fat.
moves.about: whether the baraita's principle implies that a kidney entirely covered in its fat imparts no impurity

moves.cueHe: תא חזי כמה חוטין נמשכין הימנה
moves.summary: Rava: sinews run out of the kidney and can be touched.
moves.about: sinews extend outward from the kidney and can be touched, so it is not a case of what cannot be touched

moves.summary: Rav Oshaya asks about a bone one intends to perforate but has not perforated.
moves.about: whether a thigh bone one intended to perforate but has not yet perforated still counts as sealed

moves.summary: He resolves it himself: lacking perforation is not lacking an action.
moves.about: he resolves his own dilemma: lacking perforation is not considered lacking an action, so a bone he means to perforate already conveys impurity
